analysis.title: Capri Holdings (CPRI) F2Q27 Earnings Review: 2Q beat and FY27 raise; focus still on MK recovery
key_insights: CPRI F2Q27 adjusted EPS of $0.42 reported vs GS/FactSet consensus of $0.21. FY27 adj. EPS guidance raised to $2.20 from $2.15 and revenue guidance to ~$3.42bn from ~$3.40bn.

2Q sales declined -5.5% Y/Y (-4.9% ex-FX) vs GS/consensus of -9.0%/-8.1%. The beat was more modest (-7.8% vs consensus -8.1%) after adjusting for a ~$20mn wholesale shipment timing shift from 3Q into 2Q.

Jimmy Choo 2Q sales rose +11.5% Y/Y (+7.6% excluding the timing shift) vs GS/consensus of +2.9%/+3.1%, led by the Americas and EMEA. FY27 Jimmy Choo revenue outlook raised to ~$650mn from ~$635mn, segment margin forecast kept at LSD%.

Michael Kors 2Q sales declined -8.6% Y/Y (-10.6% adjusted for timing) vs GS/consensus of -11.1%/-10.9%. Management cited sequential improvement each month of the quarter as fall product arrived and inventory constraints eased, with early reads on TikTok Shop and select new styles lifting full-price selling.

Management targets a return to growth at Michael Kors in 4Q. GS expects investor focus on further improvement as the company cycles last year's quality-of-sales initiatives and delayed product flows from supply chain constraints.

Gross margin of 63.3% expanded ~230bps Y/Y, above consensus of 63.0% but below GSe of 64.0%, driven by higher full-price sell-through, brand mix and lower tariff rates Y/Y. Adjusted EBIT margin of 3.8% vs GS/consensus of 1.4%.

3Q guidance: adj. EPS ~$0.95 in line with GS/consensus of $0.94/$0.93, but sales ~$1.005bn and operating income ~$90mn are below consensus ($1.012bn/$1.019bn sales, $108.3mn/$109.6mn operating income). The sales guide includes the ~$20mn timing shift out of 3Q.

FY27 adjusted operating income guidance raised to ~$175mn from ~$170mn vs GS/consensus of $165.7mn/$167.4mn. Guidance assumes an incremental 10% tariff rate through July 24, 2026 and 10%-12.5% thereafter.
FY27 share repurchases raised to ~$300mn from ~$200mn. GS cites the larger buyback as an additional positive driver and as part of the lower share count in its estimates.
GS keeps a Neutral rating and raises its 12-month price target to $20 from $18 (7.1% upside from $18.68), rolling forward its Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA methodology with the target multiple unchanged at 6.25x.
GS FY27/FY28/FY29 EPS estimates raised to $2.22/$2.52/$3.05 from $2.13/$2.34/$2.82, reflecting stronger 2Q trends, timing shifts, modest profitability changes and a lower share count.
Key debate is execution: sustaining brand momentum, broadening it beyond a few core franchises, and driving an inflection to growth in the Outlet channel.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised to $20 from $18 as GS rolls its EV/EBITDA valuation forward on higher estimates at an unchanged 6.25x multiple. Rating stays Neutral, with the Michael Kors recovery still the focus.

risk_factors: Upside risks: faster sales recovery and growth, faster margin recapture from improving brand heat, stronger cash flow generation.
Downside risks: a longer path to sales improvement, sustained margin compression, balance sheet and free cash flow deterioration.
Tariff assumptions in guidance: incremental 10% rate through July 24, 2026 and 10%-12.5% thereafter.
Execution risk in sustaining Michael Kors momentum beyond a few core franchises and in the Outlet channel.
